column1: # aes-r4-subfunctions.tsv -- every AES opcode and every sub-function this
# harness can put on both machines without stopping the run.
# Format (seven tab separated columns):
#   opcode  n_intin  n_intout  n_addrin  n_addrout  intin values  comment
# as cases/aes-r1.tsv, aes-r2-wind.tsv, aes-r2b-rlist.tsv and
# aes-r3-wind-state.tsv, read by the same loader (core/cases.c).  A '+'
# opcode is a PRELUDE: issued after the reset and before the measured call,
# never recorded.  A case id is the PHYSICAL LINE NUMBER and this file's
# CRC binds every dump to it, so ANY edit -- an appended case, a fixed typo
# in a comment -- invalidates every dump already taken with it.  This file
# is written ONCE.
# Built from docs/api/aes/_full-function-inventory.md (79 opcodes, 29 with
# sub-functions, 176 discrete sub-function values, ~15 fallback classes,
# 2 opcode error classes), against references/emutos @
# 1a7484aba1bfba23e2c0899e243b6d8177fe41df.
# VERSION DELTA, DECLARED BEFORE ANYTHING IS MEASURED
# The EmuTOS side is the 1.4 RELEASE ROM (etos512de.img); the pinned source
# is LATER.  git log VERSION_1_4..1a7484ab -- aes/ include/aesdefs.h
# include/obdefs.h include/gemdefs.h yields exactly TWO commits, so this is
# the complete list of AES differences between the measured ROM and the
# cited source:
#   * acb7f3b4 (2025-08-23) -- WF_OWNER (20) in wm_get (gemwmlib.c:1578-1589).
#     The 1.4 ROM has NO arm for it: field 20 falls into wm_get's
#     "default: return FALSE" (:1591-1592), so RET_CODE comes back 0 and
#     int_out[1..4] hold whatever xif's UNINITIALISED stack buffer held
#     (gemsuper.c:429-432, copy-back :444-445).  Cases 20-1, 20-2 and 20-3
#     below are therefore a VERSION DELTA on the EmuTOS side, not a defect,
#     and the four words have no target value at all on that side.
#   * 4b0d9518 (2025-08-20) -- the "nicelines" heuristic gained && (len > 3)
#     (gemoblib.c:838).  The 1.4 ROM draws a DISABLED G_STRING of 1 to 3
#     dashes as a solid line, the pinned source does not.  It affects
#     objc_draw (42) only, which this table does not issue (it needs a real
#     OBJECT tree; see THE POINTER WALL below).  Recorded here so nobody
#     later counts it as missing coverage.
# Everything else in aes/ is byte-identical between the two.
# WHY THE FREE OPCODE NUMBERS ARE NOT IN THIS FILE
# first thing an inventory-driven table wants, and they are the one thing it
# may not have.  TWO independent reasons, both checked rather than assumed:
#   1. THE ALERT BLOCKS.  crysbind's default arm runs
#      fm_show(ALNOFUNC, &opcode, 1) for every opcode != 0
#      (gemsuper.c:411-417).  fm_show -> fm_alert (gemfmlib.c:389-400) ->
#      fm_do (gemfmalt.c:383), and fm_do is a while(cont) loop around
#      ev_multi(MU_KEYBD|MU_BUTTON, ...) with NO timer (gemfmlib.c:300-313).
#      Nothing but a key or a click ends it.  On an unattended run that is a
#      hang, and a hang is indistinguishable from a defect in the thing
#      being measured.
#   2. THE LOADER REFUSES THEM ANYWAY.  aes_opcode_refusal (core/cases.c:566)
#      returns a reason for every opcode without an arm in crysbind, and
#      td_aes_cases_load refuses the WHOLE table -- so a file containing one
#      would not hang, it would simply never run a single case.  Verified:
#      casecheck --aes on a one-line probe with opcode 16 exits 1 with
#      "not an AES opcode ... would reach the default arm and pop a modal
#      alert (gemsuper.c:406-417)".
# OPCODE 0 IS THE EXCEPTION AND IT IS HERE.  gemsuper.c:414 skips the alert
# for it by name ("Ignore zero since some PRGs are this call"), and
# aes_opcode_refusal allows it by name.  Section 1 measures it three ways.
# THE POINTER WALL -- WHAT THIS HARNESS STRUCTURALLY CANNOT ASK
# The case table is pointer-free by construction: core/runner_aes.c poisons
# addr_in[] with the 0xDEAD pattern before every call and there is no column
# that could hold an address, because the same file has to lie on two
# machines with different memory maps.  Every opcode whose work is behind an
# addr_in pointer is therefore either unusable or usable only on the arm
# that returns BEFORE the pointer is touched.  This table takes every such
# arm it can prove safe from the source, and no other:
#   objc_add (40)       parent/child NIL guard, ob_add's
#                       "if ((parent != NIL) && (child != NIL))"
#                       (gemoblib.c) -- the tree is never dereferenced.
#   objc_delete (41)    obj == ROOT -> "return 0" before the first
#                       tree[obj] (gemoblib.c).  ROOT AND NOTHING ELSE:
#                       ob_delete has NO guard for a NEGATIVE object, so
#                       objc_delete(-1) would read tree[-1] through the
#                       poison and bus-error a TT in supervisor mode.  It is
#                       deliberately absent.
#   objc_order (45)     mov_obj == ROOT -> "return FALSE" before
#                       get_par (gemoblib.c:1208-1209).
#   objc_edit (46)      "if ((kind == EDSTART) || (obj <= 0)) return TRUE;"
#                       (gemobed.c:342-343) -- all five kind classes are
#                       reachable through the obj <= 0 half.
#   menu_register (35)  pid < 0 -> "return -1" before pstr is stored
#                       (gemmnlib.c:794,817).
#   menu_bar (30)       showit == 0 takes the else arm, which never touches
#                       the tree (gemmnlib.c:724-728).
#   appl_tplay (14)     length 0 -> the for loop never runs, pbuff never
#                       dereferenced (gemaplib.c:126).
#   shel_get/put        len 0 -> memcpy of zero bytes (gemshlib.c).
#   graf_mouse (78)     every mode except USER_DEF overwrites maddr before
#                       gsx_mfset (gemgrlib.c:426-449).
#   rsrc_saddr (113)    an unknown rstype -> get_addr returns (void *)-1L
#                       and rs_saddr returns FALSE WITHOUT writing
#                       (gemrslib.c:727-739).  That one arm, and no other.
# Named and NOT here, because no arm of them is reachable without a real
# pointer: objc_draw 42, objc_find 43, objc_offset 44, objc_change 47,
# form_center 54, form_keybd 55, menu_icheck 31, menu_ienable 32,
# menu_tnormal 33, menu_text 34, appl_find 13, appl_write 12,
# scrp_read 80, scrp_write 81, rsrc_load 110, rsrc_obfix 114,
# shel_read 120, shel_find 124, shel_envrn 125, wind_get/set WF_NAME 2 and
# WF_INFO 3, wind_set WF_NEWDESK 14, graf_mouse USER_DEF 255.
# scrp_read (80) and scrp_write (81) deserve a sentence of their own: the
# loader lets them through (core/cases.c's aes_opcodes[] has NULL for both)
# but sc_read does strcpy(pscrap, D.g_scrap) and sc_write does
# strcpy(D.g_scrap, pscrap) (gemsclib.c) straight through the poisoned
# pointer.  On a TT 0xDEADDEAD is outside every RAM bank, so that is a
# supervisor-mode bus error.  They are kept out by this file, not by the
# guard.
# rsrc_gaddr WITHOUT A LOADED RESOURCE -- WHAT IS AND IS NOT DECIDABLE
# Section 4 walks all 17 R_* types.  It has to do so on a dumper that has
# NOT loaded a resource, because rsrc_load (110) takes its filename through
# addr_in[0] and this table has no pointer to give it.  What that means is
# stated here rather than discovered later:
#   appl_init does NOT set ap_ptree or ap_rscmem (gemsuper.c:92-98 writes
#   ap_version, ap_count, ap_id, ap_private, ap_planes, ap_3resv and nothing
#   else), and the dumper's AESGLOBAL is a zero-initialised static
#   (core/gem.c).  Both machines have already logged it:
#   reference/EMUTOS14-AES.LOG and reference/NEWTOS-AES.LOG both show
#   global[5..8] = 0,0,0,0, i.e. ap_ptree == NULL and ap_rscmem == NULL.
#   So rs_sglobe sets rs_hdr = NULL (gemrslib.c:677-678) and get_addr
#   computes (char *)0 + hdr->rsh_xxx + size*index (gemrslib.c:100-105),
#   reading its offsets out of the m68k exception vector table.  The call
#   runs in supervisor mode, so nothing faults; but the ADDRESS it hands
#   back is a function of low memory and has no target value.
#   WHAT IS STILL DECIDABLE, and is why the section is here anyway:
#     * the RETURN CODE per type -- rs_gaddr returns (*rsaddr != -1L)
#       (gemrslib.c:717-722), so every type with a case arm answers TRUE and
#       only an unknown type answers FALSE.  That is the fallback class.
#     * THE THREE IDENTITY PAIRS.  R_TEDINFO 2 == R_TEPTEXT 8,
#       R_ICONBLK 3 == R_IBPMASK 11, R_BITBLK 4 == R_BIPDATA 14 share a
#       case label in get_addr (gemrslib.c:126-137), so they compute the
#       SAME expression and must return the SAME addr_out[0] -- a comparison
#       INSIDE one machine's own run, independent of what that address is.
#       Measured at index 0 and again at index 1, which also makes the
#       per-type record stride visible.
#     * the stride between index 0 and index 1 per type.
#   WHAT IS NOT: the absolute addr_out[0] value.  It is recorded, not
#   compared away; a reader must not treat a difference there as a defect.
# rsrc_saddr (113) is NOT walked over the 17 types, and that is a safety
# decision with a citation: rs_saddr does *psubstruct = rsaddr
# (gemrslib.c:734) where psubstruct is the same low-memory address get_addr
# computed and rsaddr is the 0xDEAD poison.  That writes 0xDEADDEAD into the
# m68k exception vector table or the OS variables below 0x800.  The run
# would not finish and the machine would not survive it.  Only the
# unknown-type arm, which returns before the store, is measured.
# WHAT THE LOADER REFUSES THAT THE INVENTORY WANTS -- REPORTED, NOT WORKED AROUND
# core/cases.c's refusal guard is written for "TOS 3.06 = AES 3.20"
# (its GATED reason cites config.h:1345-1354).  The machines actually
# measured are not that: both logs show ap_version 0340, and config.h's own
# ladder makes 0x0340 mean CONF_WITH_3D_OBJECTS && CONF_WITH_MENU_EXTENSION
# && CONF_WITH_WINDOW_COLOURS && CONF_WITH_GRAF_MOUSE_EXTENSION all set.
# Four groups are therefore refused by the loader although the reference
# ROM has them, and they are absent from this table for that reason alone:
#   objc_sysvar (48)  -- 11 sub-function values (6 which x get/set, minus
#                        the AD3DVALUE set arm) plus 2 fallback classes.
#                        The single biggest hole in this table.
#   appl_yield (17)   -- dsptch(), no parameters, provably non-blocking.
#   evnt_multi (25)   -- refused at opcode granularity, although
#                        MU_TIMER with tmcount == 0 takes the "quick check
#                        timer" arm and returns without ever reaching mwait
#                        (gemevlib.c:222-226).
#   form_error (53)   -- refused at opcode granularity, although n > 63
#                        returns FALSE before fm_show (gemfmlib.c:441-443).
# Taking an opcode off that list is a source change with a citation, which
# is the guard's stated design.  This file does not do it; the gap is
# reported instead.
# SAFETY -- WHAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE THIS FILE WAS WRITTEN
#  * No blocking opcode.  Every opcode here has refusal == NULL in
#    aes_opcodes[], and for the ones whose hazard is in the PARAMETERS the
#    safe arm is cited above.
#  * No opcode that ends or replaces the application: no appl_exit 19, no
#    shel_write 121 in any doex (0 and 1 leave the program, 4 and 5 are
#    system-wide), no scrp_clear 82.
#  * TWO distinct wind_open handles over the whole file, 1 and 2, against
#    the loader's bound of four; each open sends the dumper one WM_REDRAW
#    it never reads, unioned per handle (gemqueue.c:45-56), so two of the
#    queue's eight slots are the worst case.
#  * Every rectangle that reaches the screen is non-negative and lies
#    inside 640x400 including its drop shadow.
#  * THE MOUSE-CONTROL LEDGER.  wind_update END_MCTRL (2) drives ml_ocnt to
#    -1 and wm_new only drains it while (ml_ocnt > 0) (gemwmlib.c:1880), so
#    the reset does NOT heal it.  The one END_MCTRL case here carries a
#    BEG_MCTRL prelude.  BEG_MCTRL (3), mode > 3 and mode < 0 all leave a
#    POSITIVE count, which the reset does drain, so they stand alone.
#    The screen-sync half (0 and 1) heals either way, because unsync returns
#    early at sy_tas <= 0 (gemflag.c:104-108).
#  * THE CURSOR LEDGER.  graf_mouse M_OFF (256) and M_ON (257) are counting
#    (gsx_moff/gsx_mon, gemgsxif.c), nothing in the reset restores the
#    count, and there is no postlude in this format.  So M_OFF is the
#    second-to-last case of the file and M_ON is the last, in that order:
#    0 -> 1 -> 0 over the whole run, and nothing after them can be
#    affected.
#  * evnt_dclick (26) with setit != 0 writes gl_dcindex, which no reset
#    restores.  The read-back case carries its own set as a PRELUDE rather
#    than relying on the case before it, so a partial run still measures
#    what the line says.  rate 3 is inside gl_dcrates[5] (gemevlib.c:33);
#    EmuTOS does not range-check it and an out-of-range rate has no target
#    value, so none is issued.
#  * menu_bar (30) with show 0 clears gl_mntree (gemmnlib.c:726) and nothing
#    in the run restores it.  It is in the last section, after every case
#    that could care, and it changes no return value of any of them.
#  * No wind_open(0), no wind_delete(0), no wind_set on handle 0, and no
#    wind_get/wind_set field carrying a pointer (2, 3, 14) or an unchecked
#    gadget index (18, 19) -- the loader refuses all of those and this file
#    does not try them.
# WHAT IS DEVICE DEPENDENT
# The TT runs 640x480, QEMU raspi4b runs 640x480, a real Pi 4 may run
# 1920x1080.  Every rectangle answer carries wm_calc's border arithmetic on
# gl_wbox / gl_hbox, and wind_find, WF_SCREEN and graf_handle are device
# parameters outright.  Those are RECORDED, not compared away.  What the
# sub-function questions decide on is narrower and device-free: which arm
# answered (RET_CODE 1 against 0), which words were written against which
# stayed 0xDEAD, and -- for the rsrc_gaddr identity pairs -- whether two
# cases of the SAME run agree.
# opcode\tn_intin\tn_intout\tn_addrin\tn_addrout\tintin\tcomment
!reset

# DECLARES is half of the measurement: xif copies exactly OUT_LEN words
# back out of a local int_out it never initialised (gemsuper.c:430-432,
# :444-445), so OUT_LEN 0 must leave the caller's poison standing and
# OUT_LEN 1 must deliver the -1.

opcode 0, OUT_LEN 0: the -1 is computed and never delivered
